confidence_notes: I ran one cost-of-living search for Havana, and it returned no usable item prices. The aggregator sites I found disagreed with each other, and some quoted the old CUC currency, which was phased out in 2021. So the food and drink anchors are model estimates from general knowledge of tourist-facing private restaurants (paladares) and bars that charge in USD or at informal exchange rates. Cuba has several exchange rates and high inflation, so local-currency prices are very volatile, and USD-equivalent prices for visitors are uncertain. I estimated the cocktail from Havana's typically cheap rum-based drinks. I estimated wine from the price relationship to beer, because wine is mostly imported and costs more. The accommodation anchors are holistic estimates. Havana has few true registered hostels, and many budget stays are casas particulares, so the hostel and 1-star figures are uncertain. The 3-star figure reflects state and joint-venture hotels, which are poor value for the price.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on tourist-facing prices in Havana's private paladares and casas particulares, cross-checked against Caribbean and Central American comparables such as Santo Domingo and Managua. I adjusted upward for import scarcity and the effects of the embargo.
